# Twitter / X — 2008

**The account's first year, and it did not exist in this wiki until
2026-09-02.** The archive previously began on 2009-10-20; a backend fetch
recovered 213 earlier tweets, 95 of them from 2008.

The account opens on **24 September 2008** with *"i fucking looove winter
park. this town is unreal."* Winter Park is where Full Sail is. The account
is not a diary someone started and later pointed at a new life — it **begins
at the arrival**, and the second tweet, forty-five minutes later, says what
the arrival was for: *"Really feels like life has started over now. It's
weird enjoying life again. So stoked."*

What follows is student life at close range. Orientation on 22 October, then
the 7am starts (*"getting accustomed to getting up this early. i'll be doing
it for a month evvvvvery day. FUCK."*), twenty-hour class days, the labs, the
maths requirement he resents (*"why am i learning fucking ALGEBRA again. gb2
fourth grade."*, and the folk claim *"Fact 90% of full sail students fail
math"*), and the final on 18 December — *"Killed it. Packing to go home :("*.

Three other threads run through it. **Gear and a first studio**: a Korg
padKONTROL on 8 October, and on 12 November *"Living room is now a makeshift
studio"*. **Emo and pop-punk at saturation** — All Time Low, The Maine, Cobra
Starship, Hit The Lights, Forever The Sickest Kids, Panic, The Starting Line,
Fall Out Boy at the House of Blues on 12 December, and Hey Monday twice,
including flying back to Orlando early on 28 December to catch them. And
**World of Warcraft**, closing the year on 31 December with *"in the past 24
hours, i've played 14 hours of world of warcraft."*

Pennsylvania is already the place he does not want to be: *"I don't want to go
to cold, lame PA"* and *"i fucking hate going home"*, both 19 December.

## Seven shows in ninety-eight days, and the concert log holds four

Cross-read against [[wiki/interests/concert-record/index]] on 2026-09-04.

Autumn 2008 is the densest live-music stretch in the archive, and reading it
against the concert table shows what each record is actually good for. The
table was compiled from ticket stubs and order numbers; this feed was written
from inside the venues.

| Date | Show | Concert table | The tweet |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 Oct | The Roots | absent | *"at the roots show. i can dig that."* |
| 18 Oct | All Time Low / The Maine | row 28 | *"all time lowww/the maine"* |
| 13 Nov | Cobra Starship / Hit The Lights / Forever The Sickest Kids | absent | *"cobras/hit the lights/ftsk"* |
| 15 Nov | Trans-Siberian Orchestra | absent | *"trans-siberian orchestra tonight."* → *"wow that was SUPER lame."* |
| 17 Nov | Jedi Mind Tricks | row 26 | *"holy fuck, jedi mind tricks are so fucking scary."* |
| 12 Dec | Fall Out Boy / TAI / We The Kings | row 29 | *"fall out boy/TAI/WTK - @houseofblues"* |
| 28 Dec | Hey Monday | row 36, undated | *"Flying to Orlando for hey monday tomorrow."* |

**Trans-Siberian Orchestra is the one that matters.** It is the only show in
the corpus with a recorded verdict and no ticket: announced at 17:04 Eastern,
dismissed at 23:07 — *"wow that was SUPER lame."* — and never entered into the
log he compiled later. The concert table is a record of what he decided to
attend; a feed is a record of what the evening turned out to be, and the two
diverge exactly where a night disappointed.

**Hey Monday dates the year's last movement.** On 19 December, at the airport
and hating it, he says *"Be back on the 28th for hey Monday :)"* — the return
is planned before the departure. On 27 December at 19:40 Eastern, *"Flying to
Orlando for hey monday tomorrow. Wooo"*, then *"Hate airport days."* at 10:38
on the 28th. He cut a Pennsylvania Christmas short for one show in a small
room. The concert table's row 40 — a single general-admission BACKBOOTH ticket
for 28 December 2008, filed under There For Tomorrow — is very probably the
same night under the other band's name; see the narrowed gap on the concert
index for what that join does and does not establish.

## Nicotine has an onset date, and it is not in the health pages

[[wiki/health/chemical-architecture]] lists nicotine as the stack's "ritual
regulator" and says outright that the row "has no ledger entries at all and
remains description." **This year is the description's first dated
contradiction, and it is eighteen years old.**

- **16 October 2008**, age nineteen: *"I think I'm gonna stop smoking
  cigarettes. Another problem solved."*
- **22 December 2008**, sixty-seven days later: *"coffee and cigarettes- the
  cure for a ROUGH night."*

He is already a smoker before the account opens, the first documented quit
attempt in the corpus fails inside ten weeks, and the sentence announcing it
— *"Another problem solved"* — has the whole architecture in it: the decision
is treated as the solution, and the behaviour is not consulted. A tweet of
**28 December 2017** supplies the other end, dating the beginning to a
promotional Fall Out Boy show in **2007**: *"Smoked my first pack of cigarettes
when I went to this promotional fall out boy show in 2007."* That places
nicotine onset in the same year the health pages already date the first opiate
— see [[wiki/timeline/periods/dark-era-2007-2008]] — and 2008's other intake
line, *"7 hookahs last night, throat = deaaad"* (9 December), sits in the same
register.

## The Office is not a programme here, it is the vocabulary

The account's third tweet, forty-five minutes into the archive, is *"schrute
farms is now completely wireless."* — the Winter Park apartment, named for a
beet farm in a sitcom. On 24 October the new kitten's shortlist is *"ari,
dwight, or mose?"*: two Office characters and one Entourage agent. On 5
December, *"oooomg dwight marries angela. fucking awesome."* On 25 September,
*"So amped for the office. Life is gooood."*

The show is doing something none of the other 2008 interests do — it is
supplying the words he uses for his own life rather than being a thing he
watches. That is why [[wiki/interests/the-office]] keeps turning up in years
where nothing about television is happening: *"remember when he stole 'shut up
Oscar!' from us in s5"* to Eric Jester in 2010, and *"there's 100 dogs at the
office"* in 2011, which is a pun that only lands because the phrase is already
load-bearing.

## Gaps

**This page is a lower bound, and the shortfall is structural.** The fetch that
produced it was search-based and capped at ten results per query. Every month
that returned ten hits is truncated at ten: **October, November and December
2008 are all incomplete.** Only 24 September is a strong candidate for a
complete day, at six tweets.

> **GAP CLOSED [2026-09-03]:** this section previously read *"the account's
> creation datetime was not retrievable"*, and gave 24 September 2008 as an
> inference from the earliest surviving tweet. Dan settled it himself in 2010,
> twice, by posting the output of two account-age novelty sites:
>
> | Date | Tweet | Implied creation |
> |---|---|---|
> | 2010-08-24 | *"I joined twitter 699 days ago"* | 2008-09-24 |
> | 2010-12-09 | *"I joined Twitter on the 23rd of September 2008, making my account 807 days old"* | 2008-09-23 |
>
> The one-day spread is a timezone boundary, and it resolves in favour of the
> **23rd, local time**: the earliest surviving tweet is 2008-09-24 04:52 UTC,
> which is 00:52 on the 24th in New York — so an account opened on the evening
> of the 23rd produces a first tweet dated the 24th in UTC, and the 2022
> `#MyTwitterAnniversary` post on 24 September is consistent with either.
> *"proud member of the 'twitter since 08 club'"* (2010-08-24) independently
> rules out a later year. `wiki/self/twitter/2010`.
>
> The backend user lookup did return an id (`16430736`) and no `created_at`;
> that is still true and is why the date had to come from elsewhere.

**The month-level shortfall is unchanged.** A complete X account export is
still the only thing that would fill in the truncated October, November and
December.

This page is the text archive. Every original and every reply retrieved for
the year is below, oldest first.
